why: A says the model aloud as it appears ('Y equals A E to the power minus N X'); B writes the model line while the voice only reads the question, so the student sees a formula nobody mentions. A's margin note 'The graph gives ln A, not A' is also plainer than B's 'Un-log both read-offs'.
notes: Scores are for the pick with fixed_beats applied (assemble.mjs swaps them in).
Beat 1 never says 'Find A and N' (it is printed in the question). Acceptable.
Beat 3 'This is Y equals M X plus C' uses spoken 'Y' for ln y right after 'L N Y' — a weaker student may hear the same Y. His notes use Y = mX + c, so kept.
Beats 4 and 5 wrote the whole line on the first cue, so '= 2' and 'c = −1' appeared before the voice said them. Fixed: each token on its own words (as B did).
Trap (beat 6) is plain and placed where the sign bites.
